papers.summary: Introduces decoupled nuclear-norm spectral weight decay that additively shrinks singular values, lowers effective rank, improves SVD compression, and reduces memorization under label noise.
papers.relevance: Directly matches spectral regularization, low-rank compressibility, effective rank, and noisy-label generalization.

evidence.quote: Across 124 M to 500 M LLaMA models trained with Adam-family optimizers, the resulting low-effective-rank structure improves post-training compression under matched validation-loss budgets.
At 500 M and a 4% distortion budget, we obtain 1.89× compression and 1.18× GPU inference speedup.
At 60% label noise, mean clean-test accuracy gains over matched ℓ2 regularization reach 17.78 points on MNIST and 4.59 points on four BERT-base tasks.

papers.title: Spectral Weight Decay: Inducing Low-Rank Structure in Neural Network Weights

papers.summary: Proposes sMuon, a matmul-only approximation of Muon for LoRA, and evaluates it on SFT and ReLoRA pretraining against AdamW and other low-rank Muon variants.
papers.relevance: Directly addresses optimization geometry and practical training of LoRA and other low-rank parameterizations.

evidence.quote: We derive a method for training LoRA adapters with Muon by taking a first-order approximation of the spectral-norm-regularized steepest descent objective.
In the ReLoRA pretraining setting, we illustrate that Muon LoRA methods are generally stronger than AdamW LoRA.
Our method attains the lowest final validation loss, tying with Riemannion, but being ∼30% faster.

papers.title: Approximate Muon with low-rank adapters

papers.summary: Introduces NoRA and NoRA-init, which normalize LoRA's down-projection during training or only at initialization to improve conditioning, convergence, stability, and resistance to forgetting.
papers.relevance: Strong match for LoRA optimization, parameter-efficient fine-tuning, and the geometry of low-rank updates.

evidence.quote: NoRA continuously normalizes the down-projection matrix A along the low-rank dimension throughout training.
NoRA-init normalizes A only once at initialization and subsequently optimizes it without constraints during training.
These benefits require neither additional trainable parameters nor inference-time computation.

evidence.quote: a lightweight first-stage relevance filter developed for Parlant 4.0 that removes at least 30% of candidate policies before downstream evaluation while preserving high recall.
S&Q achieves higher precision than top-K and cosine-threshold retrieval at every evaluated recall level.

evidence.quote: Recent work addresses these limitations by tightly coupling step-by-step reasoning with interactive search, treating retrieval as an action within an iterative agentic loop rather than a one-shot preprocessing step.
We analyze these systems through four architectural axes: retrieval coupling, controller design, knowledge source, and grounding strictness.
